book_prompt_example: Four objects from a museum's open collection, each one photographed as a specimen on black. Make them into a short manual: what the objects are, how to ask a model for a plate, and how to keep a set of plates looking like one book.
house_look: Photoreal specimen photograph for a printed catalogue: the object alone on a pure, flat, seamless black ground, one large soft key light from above left, a thin rim light from behind, no fill light, a deep clean shadow under the object, true-to-life colour and material, 100 mm macro lens at eye level, sharp focus across the whole object, generous empty black space around it. An unedited real photograph, not a render: no CGI look, no plastic surfaces, no glow, no halo, no sparkles, no props, no hands, no text, no labels.
delimiter_book: Context for the whole series (do not draw any text):
cover: Cover plate. Rephotograph the object from image 1 as a single specimen: keep its exact shape, proportions, colours, material, carving and surface wear; remove the original backdrop, table, museum labels and rulers. Place it small and centred in the frame, slightly below the middle, with wide empty black above and around it.
plate: Plate. Rephotograph the object from image 1 as a specimen: keep its exact shape, proportions, colours, material and details; remove its backdrop, table, museum labels and rulers. Show only this one object. Three-quarter view, centred, the object filling about half of the frame.
group: Group plate. The objects from image 1, image 2 and image 3 together on one pure black ground, set apart in a loose row like specimens laid out on a museum tray, each keeping its exact shape, colours and material, each scaled so all three read clearly, lit exactly as in image 1. Nothing else in the frame.
